<!-- pr-reviewer: 4d9922b1e3efb4d00f988051abda8c5aa8ea9792 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge** (CPU tests and shader validation only; GPU paths NOT exercised on this machine, see below).

### What looks good
- Ortho ray law is right and matches `Camera::ray_through`/`mvp`: every ray is `fwd`; origin = `eye + right*(u*h*aspect) + up*(v*h)` on the eye plane, with `h = ortho_half_height()` (the same `dist*tan(30deg)` the matrix uses). Perspective path is unchanged (`ray` returns `(eye, ray_dir)`; shader else-branch is the old expression verbatim).
- One law in three places (CPU `PreviewCamera::ray`, `trace.wgsl` via the previously unused `world_lo.w`, `composite.wgsl` via the previously unused `frame.z`); both slots were unused before, so 0 = perspective is a safe sentinel. The composite still projects the hit through the same `mvp`, so the #604 near/far/depth 0..1 handling is untouched and consistent (hit depth is measured from the eye plane, which is where the ortho view space z=0 sits).
- `orthographic(h)` refuses non-finite/non-positive half height by name; `preview_camera` returns `None` rather than panic. Frame cache key now includes the ortho half height, so a mode switch re-traces.
- Vertex pick: `sight_origin` uses the eye in perspective, and in ortho the corner's own point on the eye plane (the parallel view ray); a corner at/behind the eye plane is not offered; finite checks present. No new unwrap/expect outside tests.
- Tests pin the change: ray parallelism/origins/depth/miss-off-footprint, all 8 stock corners landing on their traced pixel in both projections, ortho occlusion along the view direction (and the old eye-test shown to read backwards), perspective unchanged.
- No snapshot PNGs, goldens, CHANGELOG.md, build.rs, scripts, .github or dependency changes. Body has `Changelog:` lines and ends `Fixes #609` / `Fixes #610`.

### Local results (merged with upstream/main: already up to date, no conflicts)
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | builds |
| sim `stock_preview` | 11 passed |
| ui `--lib` (cwd crates/ui) | 378 passed, 1 failed, 5 ignored; the failure is `headless_run_succeeds` (see #615) |
| ui `gpu_render` | SKIPPED (no adapter) |
| ui `trace_composite` | 4 "passed" but SKIPPED: output `trace_composite: no adapter - skipped` |
| ui `trace_parity` | SKIPPED: `skip: no GPU adapter on this machine` |
| naga 30.0.1 parse + full validate (`trace.wgsl`, `composite.wgsl`) | both OK |
| clippy `-p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` | clean |

```
egui headless run failed: No suitable graphics adapter found; ... metal had no fallback adapters
```

**GPU caveat:** every GPU test requests `force_fallback_adapter: true`, which macOS Metal cannot provide, so `gpu_render`, `trace_composite` and `trace_parity` return early and report "passed" without rendering (issue #615). They are not render evidence. The `headless_run_succeeds` failure is the same environmental cause. The WGSL changes were judged by reading and naga validation only; a real-Metal (or other adapter) render check of the ortho trace and composite should follow once #615 lands.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `sight_origin` accepts `depth > 1e-9`, while `mvp` clips at near = 0.1; a corner between the two is tested but would be clipped on screen anyway, so harmless.
- `viewport.rs` is already over the ~400-line guide (1412 lines); this PR adds none to it.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
